newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says has not discussed media inquiry.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says has not discussed media inquiry.

text.p: Prime Minister John Howard on Tuesday refused to be drawn on when the Australian Government would hold a public inquiry into media ownership.
"We (Federal Cabinet) haven't discussed it yet," Howard told Perth radio station 6PR shortly before chairing a cabinet meeting in Perth.

"We might discuss that issue (today), we might not. We did make it clear before the (March) election that we'd look at the cross media rules which have become outdated by the advances in technology," Howard said.

"I can say this -- that whatever method of enquiry is adopted it will be an inquiry that enables people to put their views and an enquiry where I think people will be satisfied by the transparency of it."
Howard's Liberal-National Coalition promised before its March 2 election win to hold a full inquiry into media ownership rules laid down by the former Labor government.
These rules stop foreign investors from owning more than 25 percent of a newspaper group or 15 percent of a television group, but allows foreigners unlimited access to radio.
They also stop local companies from owning both a television company and a newspaper group in the same city.
